categories.label: Strictly necessary
categories.description: Needed for the site to work — serving the app, remembering your answers on your own device, and security. These are always active and cannot be switched off, and require no consent. They set no third-party cookies: the contact form, feedback widget and survey are protected by a self-hosted, cookieless anti-spam check — a short computation your device runs only when you submit one of them, with no third-party CAPTCHA or tracker loaded.

categories.label: Analytics
categories.description: Help us understand, in aggregate, how the tool is used so we can improve it. Off unless you turn them on. Data is aggregated and never used to identify you, and turning this off changes nothing about your card.

infrastructure.name: Cloudflare
infrastructure.role: Website hosting and CDN (Cloudflare Pages), edge compute (Pages Functions), the consented research counter database (Cloudflare D1), cookieless aggregate usage measurement (Cloudflare Web Analytics, measured at the edge with no client tag or cookie), the transactional email relay for the contact/feedback forms (Cloudflare Email Sending, called server-side at api.cloudflare.com), and edge security (per-IP rate limiting on the API routes). The anti-abuse challenge is self-hosted (an in-app proof-of-work issued and verified by our own Pages Functions) — no Cloudflare or other third-party code loads in the browser for it, so this infrastructure entry adds no Content-Security-Policy source.
infrastructure.dataProcessing: Serves all site content and runs the /api endpoints. Stores consented aggregate research counters in Cloudflare D1. Relays contact/feedback form messages to the project inbox as transactional email (relay only — the application stores no copy). Measures aggregate site usage with cookieless Cloudflare Web Analytics (no per-person identifier). May process request metadata (including IP address) transiently for delivery and security; the application does not read, log or persist it.
infrastructure.retention: Operational hosting: for the life of the service. Research data: aggregate-only counters retained per docs/privacy/retention.md (no per-person record exists). Cloudflare's own transient network/security logs per its data-processing terms.
infrastructure.dataLocation: Global — Cloudflare edge network; may be processed outside Australia.

contract.note: Cloudflare Data Processing Addendum + self-serve terms to be reviewed and filed in the restricted legal records; evidence pending (fail-closed / partial-passing) — no approval is asserted here.

infrastructure.name: GitHub
infrastructure.role: Source-code hosting, pull-request review and continuous integration via GitHub Actions. The deployed site does not contact GitHub at runtime.
infrastructure.dataProcessing: Stores the repository, issues, pull requests and CI logs, and processes contributor account data under GitHub's terms. No end-user personal data from the site flows to GitHub.
infrastructure.retention: Repository and CI history retained for the life of the project; GitHub Actions logs per GitHub defaults.
infrastructure.dataLocation: United States and global — Microsoft/GitHub infrastructure.

contract.note: GitHub Customer Terms + Data Protection Agreement to be reviewed and filed; evidence pending (fail-closed / partial-passing).

infrastructure.name: Google
infrastructure.role: Application distribution through Google Play: hosts the store listing and delivers the Android store build (apps/mobile). The deployed site and the app do not contact Google at runtime; the app's only Play touchpoint is a user-initiated store deep link handed to the operating system.
infrastructure.dataProcessing: Distributes the signed Android binary and processes install, update and store-listing interactions under the device owner's own Google account and Google's terms. No end-user personal data from the Service flows to Google; the app sends nothing to Play.
infrastructure.retention: Store listing, release history and developer-account records for the life of the listing, per Google's terms.
infrastructure.subprocessorsNote: Google publishes no Play-specific subprocessor list; platform processing occurs under Google's own privacy policy, outside the Service.
infrastructure.dataLocation: United States and global — Google infrastructure.

contract.note: Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement accepted at account registration (2026-07-26); to be reviewed and filed in the restricted legal records; evidence pending (fail-closed / partial-passing).

infrastructure.name: They Vote For You
infrastructure.role: Source of parliamentary voting-record data (party positions) via the They Vote For You API, retrieved at data-build time and compiled into the dataset. The deployed site does not contact this service at runtime.
infrastructure.dataProcessing: Public parliamentary voting-record data is retrieved from the API and compiled into the dataset. No end-user personal data is sent to the OpenAustralia Foundation.
infrastructure.retention: Raw API snapshots retained in-repo as provenance under data/source/<election>/; no personal data is involved.
infrastructure.subprocessorsNote: The OpenAustralia Foundation is a volunteer-run non-profit and publishes no formal subprocessor list. The data retrieved is public parliamentary records; no personal data is disclosed to it.

contract.note: They Vote For You API terms and ODbL-1.0 data licence to be reviewed and filed; evidence pending (fail-closed / partial-passing).

antiAbuse.mechanism: Self-hosted proof-of-work challenge (ALTCHA protocol, non-interactive / invisible)
antiAbuse.note: A self-hosted, cookieless proof-of-work challenge (the open ALTCHA protocol, issued and verified by our own Pages Functions — attributed to the Cloudflare vendor entry because that is where the verifier runs; no third-party code or endpoint is involved). It runs invisibly when a form or the survey is submitted: a short background computation on the visitor's own device, never a visual or audio puzzle, so it imposes no interactive challenge and no accessibility barrier. Each challenge is purpose-bound (research, contact or feedback) and single-use.
Server-side per-IP rate limiting on the POST /api/* routes. It is applied at the edge and presents no user-facing challenge, so it is accessible to all users.
